Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates a large left-sided pleural effusion and a prominent left parahilar/retrocardiac mass. In a 22-year-old patient, this presentation is highly characteristic of extraskeletal Ewing's sarcoma (or primitive neuroectodermal tumor) involving the chest wall or mediastinum, which frequently presents with a large associated pleural effusion.
